newsitem.title: UK: FirstBus says MMC bus constraints bearable.
newsitem.headline: FirstBus says MMC bus constraints bearable.

text.p: British bus operator FirstBus Plc said it expected to be able to comply with relative ease with a regulator's requirement last week that it divest its Midland Bluebird bus company, as well as one of four Glasgow bus operations, following a Scottish acquisition last year.

"We don't think it will be a problem selling the parts," Frances Gibson-Smith, head of investor relations at FirstBus, told Reuters. "We've still got Strathclyde, which is a good business," she added.

On Friday the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) said it was requiring FirstBus to sell its Midland Bluebird subsidiary, plus about a quarter of the Glasgow operations of Strathclyde Buses (SB), within nine months.
The move, on anti-monopoly grounds, followed FirstBus's purchase last year for 96 million stg of SB Holdings and the ensuing report by the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC).

If the group fails to make the divestments in time it will be required to sell the whole of SB, the DTI said. Gibson-Smith said the company's main concern would be that the 1,000 employees at Midland Bluebird were not put at risk by the need to sell quickly.
The ruling is not seen hitting FirstBus's wider performance which company chairman Trevor Smallwood said was "in line with market expectations", in a statement after the DTI announcement.
